meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What is the occasion?
What does that mean?

examples.text: Прости, что-то я удержаться не смог.
examples.trans: Sorry, somehow I could not hold back.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'happened', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.trans: What happened?
Nothing will happen.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'district prefect' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Там просто префект пришел, требует ребрышки.
examples.trans: The prefect just arrived out there and demands ribs.
The prefect did not eat his fill.
You should not have been rude to the prefect.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И не будет у меня звезды.
examples.trans: And I will not have a star.

examples.text: Не знаю, я на экран не смотрел особо.
examples.trans: I do not know, I did not really look at the screen.
They offered me a new job.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'есться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'ate his fill'.

related.gloss: not to ate his fill (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и наесться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and ate his fill on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют наесться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to ate his fill.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это замечательно, ты будешь первым поваром России.
examples.trans: That is wonderful, you will be the first chef in Russia.
And you wrote a culinary book.

examples.text: Рассчитали, от трех до пяти тысяч за блюдо.
examples.trans: We calculated them, from three to five thousand per dish.

examples.trans: Go ahead, shoot.

examples.trans: And I will not have a star.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Sorry, a new job?

examples.text: Прости, что-то я удержаться не смог.

examples.trans: I want to say something important.

examples.text: Я не знаю, я ничего не понял.

examples.text: Он сказал, что половину слов в меню не понял.
